The twelfth month, the fifteenth day
explanation: It came to pass in the eleventh year, in the first month, in the seventh day of the month.

question: What shall cover Egypt at Tehaphnehes?
explanation: At Tehaphnehes also the day shall be darkened: as for her, a cloud shall cover her.

question: What will God break at Tehaphnehes?
explanation: I shall break there the yokes of Egypt: and the pomp of her strength shall cease in her.

question: What does God call Nebuchadrezzar and his people?
explanation: He and his people with him, the terrible of the nations, shall be brought to destroy the land.

question: What will Nebuchadrezzar's people draw and fill the land with?
explanation: They shall draw their swords against Egypt, and fill the land with the slain.

question: What shall fall out of Pharaoh's hand?
explanation: I will break his arms, and I will cause the sword to fall out of his hand.

question: What would have bound up and strengthened Pharaoh's arm to hold a sword?
explanation: It shall not be bound up to be healed, to put a roller to bind it, to make it strong to hold the sword.

question: What will God cut off in No?
explanation: I will pour my fury upon Sin, the strength of Egypt; and I will cut off the multitude of No.

question: Which people besides Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia and Chub are named as falling with Egypt?
explanation: Ethiopia, and Libya, and Lydia, and all the mingled people, and Chub, and the men of the land that is in league, shall fall with them.

question: What cry does Ezekiel give for the day that is near?
choices: Howl ye, Woe worth the day
Rejoice, for the day is come
explanation: Prophesy and say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Howl ye, Woe worth the day! For the day is near.

question: What will the people of Ethiopia suffer 'as in the day of Egypt'?
explanation: Great pain shall come upon them, as in the day of Egypt: for, lo, it cometh.

question: What shall be in Ethiopia when the slain fall in Egypt?
explanation: The sword shall come upon Egypt, and great pain shall be in Ethiopia, when the slain shall fall in Egypt.

question: What shall be broken down when the slain fall in Egypt?
explanation: They shall take away her multitude, and her foundations shall be broken down.

question: Whose time is the near day of the LORD said to be?
explanation: The day of the LORD is near, a cloudy day; it shall be the time of the heathen.

question: In which year did the word about Pharaoh's arm come?
explanation: It came to pass in the eleventh year, in the first month, in the seventh day of the month.

question: What did all the fowls of heaven do in the great cedar?
choices: Made their nests in his boughs
explanation: All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs.

question: Who dwelt under the shadow of the great cedar?
explanation: Under his shadow dwelt all great nations.

question: Into whose hand did God deliver the lifted-up tree?
choices: The mighty one of the heathen
explanation: I have therefore delivered him into the hand of the mighty one of the heathen; he shall surely deal with him.

question: What happened to the people of the earth when the tree fell?
choices: They went down from his shadow and left him
explanation: Upon the mountains and in all the valleys his branches are fallen; all the people of the earth are gone down from his shadow, and have left him.

question: What did the beasts of the field do under his branches?
explanation: Under his branches did all the beasts of the field bring forth their young.

question: What could not hide the great Assyrian cedar?
choices: The cedars in the garden of God
explanation: The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him.

question: What did all the trees of Eden do to the Assyrian?
explanation: All the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied him.

question: Who cut the tree off and left it?
choices: Strangers, the terrible of the nations
explanation: Strangers, the terrible of the nations, have cut him off, and have left him.

question: Why did God deliver the cedar to the mighty one of the heathen?
choices: Because his heart was lifted up in his height
explanation: Because he hath lifted up himself in height, and his heart is lifted up in his height; I have driven him out for his wickedness.

question: What did God cause on the day the tree went down to the grave?
choices: A feast, and he opened the deep
A storm, and he sent a flood
A mourning, and he covered the deep for him
explanation: In the day when he went down to the grave I caused a mourning: I covered the deep for him.

question: What did the nations do at the sound of the cedar's fall?
explanation: I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to hell with them that descend into the pit.

question: Why does God make an example of the great tree?
choices: That no tree by the waters exalt itself for its height
explanation: To the end that none of all the trees by the waters exalt themselves for their height.

question: Who were comforted in the nether parts of the earth?
choices: The trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon
explanation: All the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, shall be comforted in the nether parts of the earth.

question: Which trees were not like the Assyrian's boughs?
explanation: The fir trees were not like his boughs, and the chesnut trees were not like his branches.

question: Which other trees were not like his branches?
explanation: The chesnut trees were not like his branches; nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty.

question: In which month did the word of the chapter come?
explanation: It came to pass in the eleventh year, in the third month, in the first day of the month.

question: Where was the cedar's root?
explanation: Thus was he fair in his greatness: for his root was by great waters.

question: What shall remain upon the cedar's ruin?
choices: The fowls of the heaven and the beasts of the field
explanation: Upon his ruin shall all the fowls of the heaven remain, and all the beasts of the field shall be upon his branches.

question: Among whom shall Pharaoh lie, brought down with the trees of Eden?
choices: The uncircumcised, slain by the sword
explanation: Thou shalt lie in the midst of the uncircumcised with them that be slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude.

question: Who went down to hell with the cedar?
choices: They that were his arm, who dwelt under his shadow
explanation: They also went down into hell with him; they that were his arm, that dwelt under his shadow in the midst of the heathen.

question: What did God restrain when the cedar went down to the grave?
explanation: I covered the deep for him, and I restrained the floods thereof, and the great waters were stayed.

question: Where was the cedar's top?
explanation: His height was exalted above all the trees of the field, and his top was among the thick boughs.

question: What was Ezekiel told to take up for Pharaoh king of Egypt?
explanation: Son of man, take up a lamentation for Pharaoh king of Egypt.

question: What will God spread over Pharaoh to bring him up?
explanation: I will therefore spread out my net over thee with a company of many people; and they shall bring thee up in my net.

question: What will God do with Pharaoh's flesh?
choices: Lay it upon the mountains and fill the valleys
explanation: I will lay thy flesh upon the mountains, and fill the valleys with thy height.

question: Whose sword shall come upon Egypt?
explanation: The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon thee.

question: What will God cause the rivers of Egypt to run like?
explanation: Then will I make their waters deep, and cause their rivers to run like oil.

question: Who shall lament for Egypt?
explanation: The daughters of the nations shall lament her: they shall lament for her, even for Egypt, and for all her multitude.

question: By what shall the multitude of Egypt fall?
explanation: By the swords of the mighty will I cause thy multitude to fall, the terrible of the nations.

question: What shall remain upon Pharaoh when he is left on the land?
explanation: I will cast thee forth upon the open field, and will cause all the fowls of the heaven to remain upon thee.

question: With whom is Egypt told to be laid down?
explanation: Whom dost thou pass in beauty? go down, and be thou laid with the uncircumcised.

question: What will God spoil of Egypt?
explanation: They shall spoil the pomp of Egypt, and all the multitude thereof shall be destroyed.

question: What had Pharaoh done with his feet in the rivers?
choices: Troubled the waters and fouled the rivers
explanation: Thou camest forth with thy rivers, and troubledst the waters with thy feet, and fouledst their rivers.

question: What will God water with Pharaoh's blood?
choices: The land wherein he swims, even to the mountains
explanation: I will also water with thy blood the land wherein thou swimmest, even to the mountains.

question: What will God do to the sun and the moon when Pharaoh falls?
choices: Cover the sun with a cloud and the moon gives no light
Make them shine seven times brighter
explanation: I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light.

question: Into which countries will God bring Pharaoh's destruction?
choices: Countries which he has not known
explanation: I will bring thy destruction among the nations, into the countries which thou hast not known.

question: What will God brandish before the kings?
explanation: Their kings shall be horribly afraid for thee, when I shall brandish my sword before them.

question: What will God destroy from beside the great waters?
explanation: I will destroy also all the beasts thereof from beside the great waters.

question: What will the strong among the mighty do?
choices: Speak to Pharaoh out of the midst of hell
explanation: The strong among the mighty shall speak to him out of the midst of hell with them that help him.

question: Which nation has its graves set in the sides of the pit?
explanation: Asshur is there and all her company: his graves are about him: all of them slain, fallen by the sword.

question: Who is said to lie in the pit with all her multitude round about her grave?
explanation: There is Elam and all her multitude round about her grave, all of them slain.

question: Who are named with Meshech in the pit?
explanation: There is Meshech, Tubal, and all her multitude: her graves are round about him.

question: Who is said to lie with their kings and princes in the pit?
explanation: There is Edom, her kings, and all her princes, which with their might are laid by them that were slain by the sword.

question: What did the fallen mighty lay under their heads?
explanation: They have laid their swords under their heads, but their iniquities shall be upon their bones.

question: What did they bear with them that go down to the pit?
explanation: Yet have they borne their shame with them that go down to the pit.

question: What did these nations cause in the land of the living?
explanation: Asshur and Elam caused terror in the land of the living.

question: What will God fill with Pharaoh?
choices: The beasts of the whole earth
explanation: I will cause all the fowls of the heaven to remain upon thee, and I will fill the beasts of the whole earth with thee.

question: On what day of the month did the second word of the chapter come?
explanation: It came to pass also in the twelfth year, in the fifteenth day of the month.

question: What shall be upon the bones of the fallen mighty?
explanation: They have laid their swords under their heads: but their iniquities shall be upon their bones.

question: Where is a bed set for Elam?
choices: In the midst of the slain
explanation: They have set her a bed in the midst of the slain with all her multitude.

question: What will God vex when he brings Pharaoh's destruction among the nations?
explanation: I will also vex the hearts of many people, when I shall bring thy destruction among the nations.

question: How do the kings react at Pharaoh's fall?
choices: They are horribly afraid and tremble for their life
explanation: Their kings shall be horribly afraid for thee, and they shall tremble at every moment, every man for his own life, in the day of thy fall.

question: Where are the daughters of the famous nations cast down?
choices: Unto the nether parts of the earth
explanation: Wail for the multitude of Egypt, and cast them down, even her, and the daughters of the famous nations, unto the nether parts of the earth.

question: What will God set upon Egypt's land?
explanation: All the bright lights of heaven will I make dark over thee, and set darkness upon thy land.

question: What question is put to Egypt in the second lament?
choices: Whom dost thou pass in beauty?
explanation: Whom dost thou pass in beauty? go down, and be thou laid with the uncircumcised.

question: Who else are in the pit with the princes of the north?
explanation: There be the princes of the north, all of them, and all the Zidonians, which are gone down with the slain.

question: What had Meshech and Tubal and the mighty gone down with?
explanation: They are gone down to hell with their weapons of war: and they have laid their swords under their heads.

question: Who shall see the slain and be comforted?
explanation: Pharaoh shall see them, and shall be comforted over all his multitude, even Pharaoh and all his army slain by the sword.

question: Whom did the fallen of Meshech and Tubal terrify in the land of the living?
explanation: They were the terror of the mighty in the land of the living.

question: To what is Egypt delivered in the second lament?
explanation: They shall fall in the midst of them that are slain by the sword: she is delivered to the sword.

question: Where are Asshur's graves set?
choices: In the sides of the pit
explanation: Her graves are set in the sides of the pit, and her company is round about her grave.

question: Whom do the people of a land take and set for their watchman?
explanation: When I bring the sword upon a land, if the people of the land take a man of their coasts, and set him for their watchman.

question: What does the watchman do when he sees the sword come?
choices: Blows the trumpet and warns the people
explanation: If when he seeth the sword come upon the land, he blow the trumpet, and warn the people.

question: What happens to whoever hears the trumpet and takes no warning?
choices: He is carried away to Babylon
His blood shall be upon his own head
explanation: Whosoever heareth the sound of the trumpet, and taketh not warning; if the sword come, his blood shall be upon his own head.

question: What does God say he has no pleasure in?
explanation: As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked.

question: What does God call the house of Israel to do?
explanation: Turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Israel?

question: Where had the man who came to Ezekiel escaped from?
explanation: One that had escaped out of Jerusalem came unto me, saying, The city is smitten.

question: What happened to Ezekiel's mouth before the escaped man came?
choices: It was filled with a scroll
The LORD opened it and he was no more dumb
explanation: The hand of the LORD was upon me in the evening, and had opened my mouth, until he came to me in the morning; and I was no more dumb.

question: Who did those in the wastes of Israel say inherited the land?
explanation: They that inhabit those wastes speak, saying, Abraham was one, and he inherited the land: but we are many.

question: What will happen to those in the forts and caves?
choices: They shall die of the pestilence
They shall be carried to Babylon
They shall be given the land
explanation: They that be in the forts and in the caves shall die of the pestilence.

question: What will God give to the beasts to be devoured?
choices: Him that is in the open field
explanation: Him that is in the open field will I give to the beasts to be devoured.

question: To Ezekiel, the people are like what?
choices: A very lovely song of one with a pleasant voice
explanation: Thou art unto them as a very lovely song of one that hath a pleasant voice, and can play well on an instrument.

question: From whose hand will God require the blood if the watchman does not blow the trumpet?
explanation: If the watchman blow not the trumpet, his blood will I require at the watchman's hand.

question: What did God set Ezekiel as to the house of Israel?
explanation: So thou, O son of man, I have set thee a watchman unto the house of Israel.

question: What if Ezekiel does not warn the wicked from his way?
choices: The wicked dies, and his blood is required of Ezekiel
explanation: If thou dost not speak to warn the wicked from his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.

question: What if Ezekiel warns the wicked and he does not turn?
explanation: If thou warn the wicked of his way to turn from it; if he do not turn from his way, he shall die in his iniquity; but thou hast delivered thy soul.

question: What happens when a righteous man trusts his own righteousness and commits iniquity?
choices: All his righteousnesses are not remembered
explanation: If he trust to his own righteousness, and commit iniquity, all his righteousnesses shall not be remembered; but for his iniquity he shall die for it.

question: What must the wicked do that he may live?
choices: Restore the pledge and give again what he robbed
explanation: If the wicked restore the pledge, give again that he had robbed, walk in the statutes of life, without committing iniquity; he shall surely live.

question: What becomes of the sins of the wicked who turns and does lawful and right?
choices: None shall be mentioned to him
They are written on his hand
They are laid on his son
They are carried away by a goat
explanation: None of his sins that he hath committed shall be mentioned unto him: he hath done that which is lawful and right; he shall surely live.

question: What did the people say about the way of the Lord?
explanation: The children of thy people say, The way of the Lord is not equal: but as for them, their way is not equal.

question: How does God say he will judge Israel?
choices: By the elders of the city
explanation: O ye house of Israel, I will judge you every one after his ways.

question: What sins does God charge the people in the wastes with?
choices: Neglecting the sabbath and the tithe
Eating with blood, idol worship and shedding blood
explanation: Ye eat with the blood, and lift up your eyes toward your idols, and shed blood: and shall ye possess the land?

question: What will God lay most desolate?
choices: The land, and the mountains of Israel
explanation: I will lay the land most desolate, and the mountains of Israel shall be desolate, that none shall pass through.

question: Where do the people talk against Ezekiel?
choices: In the gates of the city
By the walls and in the doors of the houses
explanation: The children of thy people still are talking against thee by the walls and in the doors of the houses.

question: What is the heart of those who hear Ezekiel's words set on?
explanation: With their mouth they shew much love, but their heart goeth after their covetousness.

question: What shall they know when it all comes to pass?
choices: That a prophet hath been among them
explanation: When this cometh to pass, (lo, it will come,) then shall they know that a prophet hath been among them.

question: On what date did the escaped man reach Ezekiel?
choices: The fifth day of the tenth month, in the twelfth year
The first day of the third month, in the eleventh year
The seventh day of the first month, in the eleventh year
The twelfth day of the tenth month, in the tenth year
explanation: It came to pass in the twelfth year of our captivity, in the tenth month, in the fifth day of the month, that one that had escaped came unto me.

question: What do the people in the wastes say besides that Abraham was one?
choices: The land is given us for inheritance
explanation: Abraham was one, and he inherited the land: but we are many; the land is given us for inheritance.

question: On what do the people in the wastes stand?
explanation: Ye stand upon your sword, ye work abomination, and ye defile every one his neighbour's wife.

question: What do the people defile that God charges?
explanation: Ye defile every one his neighbour's wife: and shall ye possess the land?

question: What does the wicked do who is taken away when the watchman blows not?
choices: He is taken away in his iniquity
explanation: If the sword come, and take any person from among them, he is taken away in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at the watchman's hand.

question: What will not make the wicked fall in the day that he turneth from his wickedness?
explanation: As for the wickedness of the wicked, he shall not fall thereby in the day that he turneth from his wickedness.

question: What will not keep the righteous alive in the day that he sinneth?
explanation: Neither shall the righteous be able to live for his righteousness in the day that he sinneth.

question: How do the people come to Ezekiel and sit before him?
explanation: They come unto thee as the people cometh, and they sit before thee as my people, and they hear thy words, but they will not do them.

question: What would happen to the pomp of the land's strength?
explanation: I will lay the land most desolate, and the pomp of her strength shall cease.

question: What did the people say they pined away in?
explanation: If our transgressions and our sins be upon us, and we pine away in them, how should we then live?

question: What shall the righteousness of the righteous not do in the day of his transgression?
explanation: The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression.

question: What do the people say to one another about Ezekiel?
choices: Come, and hear what the word is from the LORD
explanation: They speak one to another, saying, Come, I pray you, and hear what is the word that cometh forth from the LORD.

question: Who shall deliver his soul?
explanation: He that taketh warning shall deliver his soul.

question: How does the chapter say the coming judgment is certain?
explanation: When this cometh to pass, (lo, it will come,) then shall they know that a prophet hath been among them.

question: From where must Ezekiel hear the word before he warns the house of Israel?
explanation: Thou shalt hear the word at my mouth, and warn them from me.

question: What do the people show with their mouth when they hear Ezekiel?
explanation: With their mouth they shew much love, but their heart goeth after their covetousness.

question: What did the shepherds of Israel eat and wear while the flock went unfed?
explanation: Ye eat the fat, and ye clothe you with the wool, ye kill them that are fed: but ye feed not the flock.

question: What does God ask the shepherds of Israel should do?
explanation: Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?

question: What became of the sheep when they were scattered?
choices: Meat to all the beasts of the field
explanation: They were scattered, because there is no shepherd: and they became meat to all the beasts of the field.

question: Where will God feed his flock when he brings them to their own land?
explanation: I will bring them to their own land, and feed them upon the mountains of Israel by the rivers.

question: What does God say to the shepherds who fed themselves?
choices: Behold, I will reward the shepherds
Behold, I will make you kings
Behold, I am against the shepherds
Behold, I will hide the shepherds
explanation: Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against the shepherds; and I will require my flock at their hand.

question: Between whom will God judge, besides cattle and cattle?
choices: The rams and the he goats
explanation: Behold, I judge between cattle and cattle, between the rams and the he goats.

question: What will God cause to come down in his season?
explanation: I will cause the shower to come down in his season; there shall be showers of blessing.

question: What will God cause to cease out of the land?
explanation: I will make with them a covenant of peace, and will cause the evil beasts to cease out of the land.

question: Where will the flock dwell safely and sleep?
choices: In the wilderness and in the woods
explanation: They shall dwell safely in the wilderness, and sleep in the woods.

question: How had the shepherds ruled the flock?
explanation: With force and with cruelty have ye ruled them.

question: Where did God's sheep wander?
choices: Through all the mountains and upon every high hill
explanation: My sheep wandered through all the mountains, and upon every high hill.

question: Why were the sheep scattered?
explanation: They were scattered, because there is no shepherd.

question: What will God require at the shepherds' hand?
explanation: I will require my flock at their hand, and cause them to cease from feeding the flock.

question: When will God seek his scattered sheep?
choices: In the cloudy and dark day
explanation: As a shepherd seeketh out his flock in the day that he is among his sheep that are scattered; so will I seek out my sheep, in the cloudy and dark day.

question: From where will God gather his people?
choices: From the people and the countries
explanation: I will bring them out from the people, and gather them from the countries, and will bring them to their own land.

question: What will God do with the fat and the strong?
choices: Destroy them and feed them with judgment
explanation: I will seek that which was lost; but I will destroy the fat and the strong; I will feed them with judgment.

question: What had the fat cattle done to the good pasture?
explanation: Seemeth it a small thing unto you to have eaten up the good pasture, but ye must tread down with your feet the residue of your pastures?

question: What does God's flock eat and drink?
choices: What the strong have trodden and fouled
explanation: My flock, they eat that which ye have trodden with your feet; and they drink that which ye have fouled with your feet.

question: Why will God judge between the fat cattle and the lean?
choices: They thrust the diseased with side and horns
explanation: Because ye have thrust with side and with shoulder, and pushed all the diseased with your horns, till ye have scattered them abroad.

question: What will David be among the people?
explanation: I the LORD will be their God, and my servant David a prince among them.

question: What will God make the places round about his hill?
explanation: I will make them and the places round about my hill a blessing.

question: What will God raise up for them?
explanation: I will raise up for them a plant of renown, and they shall be no more consumed with hunger in the land.

question: What are the flock of God's pasture called?
explanation: And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God.

question: What shall the tree of the field and the earth yield?
explanation: The tree of the field shall yield her fruit, and the earth shall yield her increase.

question: What had the shepherds not sought?
explanation: The diseased have ye not strengthened, neither have ye sought that which was lost.

question: What will God cause his flock to do in a good fold?
explanation: I will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down, saith the Lord GOD.

question: By what will God feed his flock on the mountains of Israel?
explanation: I will feed them upon the mountains of Israel by the rivers, and in all the inhabited places of the country.

question: What had the fat cattle done to the deep waters?
choices: Fouled the residue with their feet
explanation: And to have drunk of the deep waters, but ye must foul the residue with your feet?

question: What shall none do to the flock when they dwell safely?
explanation: They shall dwell safely, and none shall make them afraid.

question: From what shall the flock be no more consumed?
explanation: They shall be no more consumed with hunger in the land, neither bear the shame of the heathen any more.

question: From whom will God deliver his people when he breaks their yoke?
choices: Those that served themselves of them
explanation: I have broken the bands of their yoke, and delivered them out of the hand of those that served themselves of them.

question: What will the people know when God is with them?
explanation: Thus shall they know that I the LORD their God am with them, and that they, even the house of Israel, are my people.

question: Where shall the fold of Israel be?
choices: Upon the high mountains of Israel
explanation: Upon the high mountains of Israel shall their fold be: there shall they lie in a good fold.

question: What will God do for that which was broken?
explanation: I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken.

question: What will God do so that his flock shall no more be a prey?
explanation: Therefore will I save my flock, and they shall no more be a prey; and I will judge between cattle and cattle.

question: How far was the flock scattered?
choices: Upon all the face of the earth
explanation: My flock was scattered upon all the face of the earth, and none did search or seek after them.

question: What will the shepherds no more do?
explanation: Neither shall the shepherds feed themselves any more; for I will deliver my flock from their mouth.

question: From what will God deliver his flock?
explanation: I will deliver my flock from their mouth, that they may not be meat for them.

question: What will God do with the sick of the flock?
explanation: I will strengthen that which was sick: but I will destroy the fat and the strong.

question: What shame will the people bear no more?
explanation: Neither bear the shame of the heathen any more.

question: What had Mount Seir done to the children of Israel?
choices: Shed their blood by the force of the sword
explanation: Thou hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity.

question: What will pursue Mount Seir?
explanation: I will prepare thee unto blood, and blood shall pursue thee: sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee.

question: Which land is named with Mount Seir in the final judgment?
explanation: Thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it: and they shall know that I am the LORD.

question: When did Edom shed the blood of Israel?
choices: In the time of their calamity
In the day of their feast
explanation: Thou hast shed the blood of the children of Israel in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end.

question: What will God cut off from Mount Seir?
choices: Him that passeth out and him that returneth
explanation: I will make mount Seir most desolate, and cut off from it him that passeth out and him that returneth.

question: What will God fill the mountains of Seir with?
explanation: I will fill his mountains with his slain men: in thy hills, and in thy valleys, and in all thy rivers, shall they fall that are slain with the sword.

question: What did Edom say of the mountains of Israel?
choices: They are holy to the LORD
They are laid desolate, they are given us to consume
explanation: Thou hast spoken against the mountains of Israel, saying, They are laid desolate, they are given us to consume.

question: What had Edom done against God with its mouth?
choices: Boasted and multiplied words against him
explanation: Thus with your mouth ye have boasted against me, and have multiplied your words against me: I have heard them.

question: How had Edom reacted to the inheritance of Israel?
choices: It rejoiced because it was desolate
explanation: As thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so will I do unto thee.

question: What will God make known among them when he has judged Edom?
explanation: I will even do according to thine anger, and according to thine envy; and I will make myself known among them, when I have judged thee.

question: What had Edom not hated, so that blood would pursue it?
explanation: Sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee.

question: Where shall those who are slain with the sword fall?
choices: In the hills, valleys and rivers
explanation: In thy hills, and in thy valleys, and in all thy rivers, shall they fall that are slain with the sword.

question: What does God say he has heard from Edom?
explanation: Thou shalt know that I have heard all thy blasphemies which thou hast spoken against the mountains of Israel.

question: When will God make Seir desolate?
explanation: When the whole earth rejoiceth, I will make thee desolate.

question: What had Edom used its anger and envy out of?
explanation: I will do according to thine anger, and according to thine envy which thou hast used out of thy hatred against them.

question: What does God say he will do to Seir's cities?
explanation: I will lay thy cities waste, and thou shalt be desolate.

question: What does God say he will stretch out against Mount Seir?
explanation: Behold, O mount Seir, I am against thee, and I will stretch out mine hand against thee.

question: What would Seir become?
explanation: I will make thee perpetual desolations, and thy cities shall not return.

question: What was Ezekiel told to do against Mount Seir?
choices: Set his face against it and prophesy
explanation: Son of man, set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it.

question: What will God sprinkle upon his people to make them clean?
explanation: Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you.

question: What will the heart of stone be exchanged for?
explanation: I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.

question: What will the desolate land be called when it is tilled?
explanation: This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden.

question: From where will God gather his people to bring them to their own land?
choices: From among the heathen and all countries
explanation: I will take you from among the heathen, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land.

question: What shall the mountains of Israel yield to God's people?
explanation: Ye, O mountains of Israel, ye shall shoot forth your branches, and yield your fruit to my people of Israel.

question: Why did God pour his fury upon the house of Israel?
choices: For the blood they had shed and for their idols
explanation: I poured my fury upon them for the blood that they had shed upon the land, and for their idols wherewith they had polluted it.

question: What did God do with Israel among the heathen?
explanation: I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries.

question: What did the heathen say of Israel that profaned God's name?
choices: These are the people of the LORD, gone forth out of his land
explanation: They profaned my holy name, when they said to them, These are the people of the LORD, and are gone forth out of his land.

question: How will God increase his people?
explanation: I will increase them with men like a flock.

question: What will God do for the corn when he saves his people?
choices: Call for it and increase it
explanation: I will also save you from all your uncleannesses: and I will call for the corn, and will increase it, and lay no famine upon you.

question: What had the enemy said against the mountains of Israel?
choices: Aha, even the ancient high places are ours in possession
explanation: Because the enemy hath said against you, Aha, even the ancient high places are ours in possession.

question: What had the heathen done to the mountains of Israel?
choices: Made them desolate and swallowed them up on every side
explanation: Because they have made you desolate, and swallowed you up on every side, that ye might be a possession unto the residue of the heathen.

question: Against whom has God spoken in the fire of his jealousy?
choices: The residue of the heathen and all Idumea
explanation: In the fire of my jealousy have I spoken against the residue of the heathen, and against all Idumea.

question: What will the heathen round about Israel bear?
explanation: I have lifted up mine hand, Surely the heathen that are about you, they shall bear their shame.

question: What does God say to the mountains of Israel about himself?
choices: I am for you, and I will turn unto you
explanation: For, behold, I am for you, and I will turn unto you, and ye shall be tilled and sown.

question: What will God do better for Israel than at their beginnings?
choices: Settle them after their old estates and do better to them
Make them a nation of priests
explanation: I will settle you after your old estates, and will do better unto you than at your beginnings.

question: What did the people say of the land that God will end?
explanation: Because they say unto you, Thou land devourest up men, and hast bereaved thy nations; therefore thou shalt devour men no more.

question: To what does God liken Israel's way when they dwelt in their own land?
choices: The uncleanness of a removed woman
explanation: When the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it by their own way: their way was before me as the uncleanness of a removed woman.

question: Why did God have pity?
explanation: But I had pity for mine holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the heathen.

question: What will God sanctify when he is sanctified in Israel?
explanation: I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned among the heathen.

question: In which land shall they dwell?
choices: The land God gave to their fathers
explanation: Ye shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; and ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.

question: What will God do to the ruined places?
choices: Build them and plant the desolate
explanation: I the LORD build the ruined places, and plant that that was desolate: I the LORD have spoken it, and I will do it.

question: What had talkers made the mountains of Israel?
explanation: Ye are taken up in the lips of talkers, and are an infamy of the people.

question: What shall be done to the mountains of Israel before they are inhabited?
choices: They shall be tilled and sown
explanation: I am for you, and I will turn unto you, and ye shall be tilled and sown.

question: What will God multiply upon the land?
explanation: I will multiply upon you man and beast; and they shall increase and bring fruit.

question: What shall the land no more do to Israel?
explanation: They shall possess thee, and thou shalt be their inheritance, and thou shalt no more henceforth bereave them of men.

question: What will God not let men hear in the land any more?
explanation: Neither will I cause men to hear in thee the shame of the heathen any more.

question: What will God multiply so that Israel receives no reproach of famine?
choices: The fruit of the tree and the increase of the field
explanation: I will multiply the fruit of the tree, and the increase of the field, that ye shall receive no more reproach of famine among the heathen.

question: What will Israel do when they remember their own evil ways?
choices: Lothe themselves in their own sight
explanation: Then shall ye remember your own evil ways, and shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations.

question: What does God tell Israel to be for their own ways?
explanation: Not for your sakes do I this, be it known unto you: be ashamed and confounded for your own ways, O house of Israel.

question: What will become of the waste and ruined cities?
explanation: The waste and desolate and ruined cities are become fenced, and are inhabited.

question: What will God yet be, for the house of Israel?
choices: Enquired of by them to do it
explanation: I will yet for this be enquired of by the house of Israel, to do it for them.

question: To what flock does God liken the waste cities filled with men?
choices: The flock of Jerusalem at her solemn feasts
The flock of the shepherds of Israel
explanation: As the holy flock, as the flock of Jerusalem in her solemn feasts; so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of men.

question: When will God cause Israel to dwell in the cities?
choices: The day he has cleansed them from all iniquities
explanation: In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities I will also cause you to dwell in the cities.

question: What will the heathen that are left round about know?
choices: That the LORD builds the ruined places
explanation: Then the heathen that are left round about you shall know that I the LORD build the ruined places.

question: What will God cause to walk upon the mountains of Israel?
explanation: I will cause men to walk upon you, even my people Israel; and they shall possess thee.

question: When will the heathen know that he is the LORD?
choices: When he is sanctified in Israel before their eyes
explanation: The heathen shall know that I am the LORD, when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes.

question: How much of the house of Israel will God multiply upon the mountains?
explanation: I will multiply men upon you, all the house of Israel, even all of it: and the cities shall be inhabited, and the wastes shall be builded.

question: What will become of the wastes when Israel returns?
explanation: The cities shall be inhabited, and the wastes shall be builded.

question: What did God lift up against the heathen who bore their shame?
explanation: I have lifted up mine hand, Surely the heathen that are about you, they shall bear their shame.

question: Who is thrown into the wilderness with Pharaoh the great dragon?
choices: All the fish of his rivers
explanation: God says, I will leave thee thrown into the wilderness, thee and all the fish of thy rivers.

question: Who will know that God is the LORD because they were a staff of reed to Israel?
explanation: All the inhabitants of Egypt shall know that I am the LORD, because they have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel.

question: What are the princes of the north and the Zidonians ashamed of in the pit?
explanation: The princes of the north and all the Zidonians, with their terror they are ashamed of their might, and bear their shame with them that go down to the pit.
